The '''2026 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election''' will take place on Thursday 7 May 2026, alongside [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]]. One third of the 45 members of [[Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council]] in [[Merseyside]] will be elected.

==Summary==
===Background===
Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council was created in 1974. Like much of Merseyside, [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] have always performed well in local elections, forming majority administrations for the entirety of the council's existence.<ref>{{cite web |title=BBC News - Election 2011 - England council elections - Knowsley |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/election2011/council/html/bx.stm |website=BBC News |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> The party have always held over 60% of the seats;<ref name=EC>{{cite web |title=Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Knowsley-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> this includes a period between [[2012 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2012]] and [[2016 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2016]] when every seat was held by Labour.

The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] formed the principal opposition from 1974 to [[1994 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election|1994]], when they were overtaken by [[independent politician|independents]]. From [[1996 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election|1996]] to 2012, the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] formed the main opposition.<ref name=EC /> [[2021 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2021]] saw the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] overtake the Liberal Democrats, and they have formed the principal opposition since.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McKeon |first1=Christopher |title=Knowsley deputy leader loses seat as opposition make gains |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/liverpool-news/local-elections-2021-knowsley-deputy-20544966 |access-date=9 January 2026 |work=Liverpool Echo |date=7 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

The seats up for election this year were last contested in [[2022 Knowsley Metropolitan Borough Council election|2022]]. That election saw Labour take 10 seats (down two), the Greens take 2 (up 1), independents take 2 (up 1), and the Liberal Democrats take 1 (steady).<ref>{{cite news |title=Knowsley result - Local Elections 2022 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/election/2022/england/councils/E08000011 |access-date=9 January 2026 |work=BBC News}}</ref>

=== Electoral process ===
The council previously elected its councillors in thirds, with a third being up for election every year for three years, with no election in the fourth year.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.gov.uk/guidance/local-government-structure-and-elections#electoral-cycles|title=Local government structure and elections|work=GOV.UK|access-date=2018-04-27|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/694598/Election_Timetable_in_England.pdf|title=Election Timetable in England}}</ref> However, following a boundary review, all forty-five councillors will be elected at the same time. The election will take place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by up to three councillors. Electors will be able to vote for as many candidates as there are seats to fill, and the candidates with the most votes in each ward will be elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in Knowsley aged 18 or over will be entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, are entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities. Voting in-person at polling stations will take place from 07:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters will be able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.
